text:
sam: Kicking off a short plan for FlashAttention v3 integration into the kernel chooser. Main objectives: validate batching heuristics, confirm KV-cache interaction for paged attention, and have automated rollbacks/safeties. TL;DR: we saw ~+24% throughput on 2k seq offline profiles but P95 is slightly higher on long-context traces so we need staged rollout.

anya: Nice. Can you paste the key perf numbers from the last profiling run?

sam: Sure — quick snapshot from local perf run (N=20 warmups):
```
model: llama-2-13B, seq=2048, batch=8
flashv2: tokens/s = 980 ± 30, p50_lat=74ms, p95_lat=210ms
flashv3: tokens/s = 1210 ± 40, p50_lat=64ms, p95_lat=245ms
paged-attn fallback: tokens/s = 650 ± 25, p50_lat=120ms, p95_lat=360ms
```
Interpretation: throughput improves but p95 widened by ~35ms on that trace set. Need to see production traces with mixed short/long prefixes; KV cache hit behavior is the suspect.

mike: Important to test with real KV-hit ratios. In prod we've got a lot of short prompts with cold-starts still. What's the plan for exercising KV eviction / snapshotting?

sam: Proposed flow:
- Add a lightweight KV snapshot on canary that records hit/miss rate per model-route (no payloads, just counts)
- Run canary 24h, compare p95 by KV_hit_bucket (0,1-5,>5)
- If p95 regresses >10% on any heavy-KV bucket, rollback to flashv2 for that route

dana: How do we flip the flag? We should use our standard feature-flagger with staged percentages and region splits. Example commands:
```bash
rosetta ff set attn.kernel=flashv3 --env=canary --percent=5 --regions=us-east-1,eu-west-1
rosetta ff set attn.kernel=flashv3 --env=staging --percent=100
```
Also add a kill-switch: `rosetta ff set attn.kernel=flashv3 --state=off --force` in case of emergency.

yusuf: Recommend these runtime safeties:
- Automatic fallback on 5xx or >2% error rate for 5m window
- Latency SLO detector: if p95 > baseline * 1.15 for 10m, switch to flashv2 for that route
- KV-miss throttle: if KV_miss_rate > 40% for the route, force paged-attn (safer)

luis: We should also protect batching. v3 is more sensitive to batch-size distribution. Suggest heuristics: prefer max_batch=16 for seq>1024, but ramp up to 24 on short seqs. Proposed config:
```json
{"batching": {"short_seq_max": 24, "long_seq_max": 16, "dynamic_window_ms": 8}}
```
This is only for canary.

anya: Good. Who owns the canary run and telemetry dashboards? I can set up the KV-hit dashboard and a bucketed p95 heatmap.

sam: Assigning: anya for telemetry, mike for canary ops, dana for ff rollout, yusuf for fallback rules, luis for batching heuristics. I'll do the integration PR and test infra changes.

deploy-bot: :rocket: canary deploy started by sam — cluster=eng-runtime-canary-1, image=runtime:flashv3-integ-20260318

mike: Quick checklist before flipping 5%:
- [x] integration PR merged
- [x] canary infra pre-provisioned
- [x] telemetry dashboards created (anya)
- [ ] smoke tests for long prefixes added to canary test suite

anya: Dashboard links (will populate once ready):
- KV hit/miss per route: https://grafana.redwood/boards/kv-hits
- p50/p95 heatmap by seq length: https://grafana.redwood/boards/attn-p95-heatmap

sam: Smoke test idea: synthetic stream with 10k requests split across seq buckets: 16/128/512/2048 and simulated KV-hit ratios 0/30/70/90. We need to ensure no silent throughput cliff.

dana: Also add a rollout note to ops-runbook: when flipping more than 20% we must notify #oncall-eng-sre and slack #incidents; include the auto-fallback commands.

sam: Auto-fallback command (ops):
```bash
# force per-route kernel back to flashv2
rosetta route update --route-id <route> --kernel flashv2
# temporarily pin batching config
rosetta route update --route-id <route> --config '{"batching": {"short_seq_max": 16, "long_seq_max": 8}}'
```

yusuf: One more gotcha: quantization path differences between v2 and v3 can expose small numerical diffs. Add a small eval set check: 500 prompts, compare logprob delta and generation diffs; gate on >1% behavioral regressions. I can script this.

luis: For metrics, capture these: tokens/sec, p50/p95 lat, KV_hit_rate, batch_size_histogram, error_rate, model-compare-regression%. We'll snapshot every 1m and store as compressed CSV.

mike: Timing: proposed schedule
- day 0: staging 100% (sanity)
- day 1: canary 5% (us-east, eu-west) 24h
- day 2: canary 20% (add ap-southeast) 24h
- day 4: ramp to 50% after ops signoff
- day 7: full roll if no regressions

anya: I'll add an alert: if any route's p95 increases by >12% and error_rate >0.5% -> auto-disable.

sam: After canary, we'll run a focused perf regression job on the 7-day production traces sampling heavier KV sequences to validate. If we see persistent p95 delta despite batching changes, we will mark v3 as "perf-unready" for that model family and revert chooser defaults.

dana: Sounds solid. Please add these notes to the PR description and link the dashboards. Also include a short troubleshooting FAQ in the runbook: common causes (KV eviction storms, batch-starvation, kernel mis-selection).

sam: Will do. I pushed a draft PR and added the rollout checklist to the PR template. Thanks everyone — starting the canary flip in ~30m.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: canary deploy completed for 5% traffic — cluster=eng-runtime-canary-1, uptime=2m

mike: Observing early metrics: tokens/s up ~22% on canary routes, p95 +28ms on sequences >1500. KV_hit_rate currently 42% on that route. Monitoring closely.

anya: Dashboard link (live): https://grafana.redwood/boards/flashv3-canary-live

yusuf: If p95 trend continues we'll trigger auto-fallback rule at 10m. I'll keep the script ready.

sam: Perfect. We'll reconvene after 24h with the full KV-bucketed report.

luis: Recording: postmortem template pre-created in case we need it.

anya: Thanks — marking this thread as the integration runbook for traceability.

sam: Closing for now, will post results. :wave:
